plan.question: Does splitting a fixed acquisition budget between zero and finite field improve interaction inference after independent source directions and affine gains are fitted?
plan.time_model: A total budget T is shared among fields. Each field measures the same four complex entries on the same 45 frequencies with equal per-entry dwell allocation. sigma0 is the per-entry circular-complex RMS for allocating all T to one full-matrix field. Allocating fraction f gives sigma_field=sigma0/sqrt(f). Independent equal white detector noise, no switching overhead, drift, or field-dependent noise prefactor is assumed. Charge calibration is known. This is a declared acquisition model, not an apparatus claim.
plan.observations: full four-entry matrix only; no comparison with a different per-entry time allocation
plan.parameters: g/.8, Ua/8, lambda_readout, lambda_source; source directions shared across fields, independent complex affine source/readout gains in each field
plan.pairing: For each truth and repetition one independent standard circular-complex noise array per field is reused across policies, multiplied by that policy's sigma_field. This couples Monte Carlo comparisons, not physical measurements between policies.
plan.information: Analytic derivatives; true Gaussian Fisher 2 Re(J^H Sigma^-1 J); project affine gains and both source-direction nuisance columns; report Ua local bound after also fitting g. Local information does not establish confidence coverage or global uniqueness.
plan.optimizer: Five frozen starts, all attempts retained; best residual selected even if a status is false, reported honestly. Feasible exact-truth residual is a diagnostic upper bound, not an extra start or fitted estimate.
plan.selection: Report all five policies and both truths. Best and minimax choices refer only to this grid, source family, noise model and 30-realization empirical experiment. No predetermined improvement claim. No uniform source-angle robustness claim.
